ex.en: Before giving evidence, witnesses in court have to take the oath (= promise to tell the truth).
ex.cn: 作证之前，证人必须当庭宣誓据实作证。

senses.def: an offensive word or phrase used to express anger, surprise, etc.; a swear word
senses.chn: （表示愤怒、惊异等的）咒骂，诅咒的话

ex.en: She heard the sound of breaking glass, followed by a muttered oath.
ex.cn: 她听到打碎玻璃的响声，接着是低声的咒骂。

senses.def: having made a formal promise to tell the truth in court
senses.chn: （在法庭上）宣誓说实话，经宣誓

ex.en: Is she prepared to give evidence on oath?
ex.cn: 她愿意宣誓据实作证吗？

ex.en: The judge reminded the witness that he was still under oath.
ex.cn: 法官提醒证人，他仍然受宣誓的约束。

senses.def: flour made from crushed oats, used to make biscuits/cookies, porridge
a pale brown colour
grain grown in cool countries as food for animals and for making flour, porridge/ oatmeal , etc.
an important part for an instrument in a piece of music which cannot be left out
refusing to change your mind or your actions in any way
the abbreviation for 'Officer of the Order of the British Empire' (an award given in Britain for a special achievement)
senses.chn: 英帝国勋位军官，英帝国官佐勋衔获得者（全写为 Officer of the Order of the British Empire，英国授予有特殊贡献者的勋章）

ex.en: She was made an OBE.
ex.cn: 她荣获英帝国官佐勋衔。

ex.en: Matthew Silk OBE
ex.cn: 英帝国官佐勋衔获得者马修 · 西尔克

senses.def: doing what you are told to do; willing to obey
senses.chn: 顺从的；忠顺的；唯命是从的

ex.en: an obedient child
ex.cn: 听话的孩子

ex.en: He was always obedient to his father's wishes.
ex.cn: 他一向顺从父亲的意愿。

senses.def: used to end a formal letter
senses.chn: （用作正式信函的结束语）您恭顺的仆人

senses.def: to do what you are told or expected to do

ex.en: to obey a command/an order/rules/the law
ex.cn: 服从指挥／命令；遵守规章／法律

ex.en: He had always obeyed his parents without question.
ex.cn: 他对父母一向绝对服从。

ex.en: 'Sit down!' Meekly, she obeyed.
ex.cn: “坐下！” 她乖乖地顺从了。

senses.def: to make sth less clear and more difficult to understand, usually deliberately
senses.chn: （故意地）混淆，使困惑，使模糊不清

a doctor who is trained in this type of medicine

senses.chn: 顺便说的话；不重要的意见

a thing that can be seen and touched, but is not alive

ex.cn: 诸如杯碟之类的日用品

ex.en: Glass and plastic objects lined the shelves.
ex.cn: 架子上排列着玻璃和塑料制品。

ex.en: There is a new device for cars that warns drivers of traffic jams ahead.
ex.cn: 有一种新的汽车装置可提醒司机前面交通拥堵。

ex.en: His kitchen is full of gadgets he never uses.
ex.cn: 他厨房里到处是他从不使用的小器具。

ex.en: 'What do you call the instrument that measures temperature?' 'A thermometer.'
ex.cn: “测量温度的仪器叫什么？” “温度计。”

ex.en: 'Have you got one of those tools for turning screws?' 'Do you mean a screwdriver?'
ex.cn: “你有拧螺丝钉的工具吗？” “你是指螺丝刀吗？”

senses.def: a person or thing that sb desires, studies, pays attention to, etc.
senses.chn: （极欲得到、研究、注意等的）对象

senses.def: an aim or a purpose

ex.en: Her sole object in life is to become a travel writer.
ex.cn: 她人生的唯一目标就是当游记作家。

ex.en: The object is to educate people about road safety.
ex.cn: 目的是教育人们注意交通安全。

ex.en: If you're late, you'll defeat the whole object of the exercise.
ex.cn: 如果你迟到了，便不能达到整个活动的目的。

ex.en: Set yourself targets that you can reasonably hope to achieve.
ex.cn: 给自己制订有望达到的指标。

ex.en: attainment targets in schools
ex.cn: 学校的成绩目标

ex.en: What is the main objective of this project?
ex.cn: 这个项目的主要目标是什么？

senses.def: a noun, noun phrase or pronoun that refers to a person or thing that is affected by the action of the verb (called the direct object), or that the action is done to or for (called the indirect object)
senses.chn: 宾语（包括直接宾语、间接宾语）

senses.def: used to say that you are willing to spend a lot of money
senses.chn: 费用不在话下；钱不成问题

ex.en: He always travels first class—expense is no object.
ex.cn: 他总是乘头等舱旅行，从不计较花费多少。

senses.def: to say that you disagree with, disapprove of or oppose sth

ex.en: Many local people object to the building of the new airport.
ex.cn: 许多当地的居民反对兴建新机场。

ex.en: If nobody objects, we'll postpone the meeting till next week.
ex.cn: 如果没有人反对，我们就把会议推迟到下周。

ex.en: I really object to being charged for parking.
ex.cn: 我非常反对收停车费。

senses.def: to give sth as a reason for opposing sth
senses.chn: 提出…作为反对的理由；抗辩说

ex.en: He objected that the police had arrested him without sufficient evidence.
ex.cn: 他抗辩说警察没有充分的证据就逮捕了他。

senses.def: the language into which a program is translated using a compiler or an assembler
senses.chn: （编译或汇编程序的）目标码，目标代码

senses.def: the act of treating people as if they are objects, without rights or feelings of their own
senses.chn: 人格物化（把人当成没有权利或感情的物体）

senses.def: to treat sb/sth as an object

ex.en: magazines that objectify women
ex.cn: 将妇女人格物化的杂志

senses.def: a reason why you do not like or are opposed to sth; a statement about this

ex.en: I have no objection to him coming to stay.
ex.cn: 我不反对他来小住。

ex.en: I'd like to come too, if you have no objection.
ex.cn: 如果你不反对，我也想来。

ex.en: The main objection to the plan was that it would cost too much.
ex.cn: 反对这个计划的主要理由是费用过高。

ex.en: to raise an objection to sth
ex.cn: 对某事提出异议

ex.en: No objections were raised at the time.
ex.cn: 当时没人提出异议。

ex.en: The proposal will go ahead despite strong objections from the public.
ex.cn: 尽管公众强烈反对，这项提案仍将付诸实施。

senses.def: unpleasant or offensive
senses.chn: 令人不快的；令人反感的；讨厌的

ex.en: objectionable people/odours
ex.cn: 讨厌的人／气味

ex.en: Why are you being so objectionable today?
ex.cn: 你今天怎么这么别扭？

senses.def: something that you are trying to achieve

ex.en: the main/primary/principal objective
ex.cn: 主要／首要／重要目标

ex.en: to meet/achieve your objectives
ex.cn: 达到／实现你的目标

ex.en: You must set realistic aims and objectives for yourself.
ex.cn: 你必须给自己确定切实可行的目的和目标。

ex.en: The main objective of this meeting is to give more information on our plans.
ex.cn: 这次会议的主要目的是进一步介绍我们的规划。

ex.en: Set yourself targets that you can reasonably hope to achieve.
ex.cn: 给自己制订有望达到的指标。

ex.en: attainment targets in schools
ex.cn: 学校的成绩目标

senses.def: the lens in a telescope or microscope that is nearest to the object being looked at
not influenced by personal feelings or opinions; considering only facts
senses.chn: 客观的；就事论事的；不带个人感情的

ex.en: an objective analysis/assessment/report
ex.cn: 客观的分析／评价／报告

ex.en: objective criteria
ex.cn: 客观标准

ex.en: I find it difficult to be objective where he's concerned.
ex.cn: 只要涉及他，我就难以做到保持客观。

senses.def: existing outside the mind; based on facts that can be proved
senses.chn: 客观存在的；基于事实的

ex.en: objective reality
ex.cn: 客观现实

senses.def: the objective case is the one which is used for the object of a sentence
a practical example of what you should or should not do in a particular situation
a person who objects to sth

ex.en: There were no objectors to the plan.
ex.cn: 没有人反对这个计划。

senses.def: a way of programming computers so that information and instructions are stored together in units called objects
senses.chn: （编程方式）面向对象的，对象式的，物件导向的

ex.en: object-oriented languages/programming
ex.cn: 面向对象语言╱程序设计

ex.en: Java is object-oriented and well structured.
ex.cn: Java 语言是面向对象的，结构良好。

senses.def: a program into which another program is translated by a compiler or an assembler
senses.chn: 目标程序；目标程式；目的程式

senses.def: a small artistic object, used for decoration
senses.chn: （装饰性的）小艺术品，小工艺品

senses.def: having a moral or legal duty to do sth
senses.chn: （道义或法律上）有义务的，有责任的，必须的

ex.en: He felt obligated to help.
ex.cn: 他觉得有义务帮忙。

senses.def: the state of being forced to do sth because it is your duty, or because of a law, etc.

ex.en: You are under no obligation to buy anything.
ex.cn: 你不必非买什么东西不可。

ex.en: She did not feel under any obligation to tell him the truth.
ex.cn: 她觉得没有义务告诉他实情。

ex.en: I don't want people coming to see me out of a sense of obligation.
ex.cn: 我不想让别人迫于无奈来看我。

ex.en: We will send you an estimate for the work without obligation (= you do not have to accept it).
ex.cn: 我们将寄上工程估算，仅供参考。

senses.def: something which you must do because you have promised, because of a law, etc.
senses.chn: （已承诺的或法律等规定的）义务，责任

ex.en: to fulfil your legal/professional/financial obligations
ex.cn: 履行法律／职业／财务责任

ex.en: They reminded him of his contractual obligations.
ex.cn: 他们提醒他注意合同规定的义务。

ex.en: We have a moral obligation to protect the environment.
ex.cn: 我们有道义责任保护环境。

senses.def: that you must do because of the law, rules, etc.
senses.chn: （按法律、规定等）必须的，强制的

ex.en: It is obligatory for all employees to wear protective clothing.
ex.cn: 所有员工必须穿防护服装。

senses.def: that you do because you always do it, or other people in the same situation always do it
senses.chn: 习惯性的；随大溜的；赶时髦的

ex.en: In the mid 60s he took the almost obligatory trip to India.
ex.cn: 60 年代中期，他也赶时髦到印度一游。

senses.def: to force sb to do sth, by law, because it is a duty, etc.

ex.en: Parents are obliged by law to send their children to school.
ex.cn: 法律规定父母必须送子女入学。

ex.en: I felt obliged to ask them to dinner.
ex.cn: 我不得不请他们吃饭。

ex.en: He suffered a serious injury that obliged him to give up work.
ex.cn: 他受伤严重，不得已只好放弃工作。

senses.def: to help sb by doing what they ask or what you know they want

ex.en: Call me if you need any help—I'd be happy to oblige.
ex.cn: 若有需要，尽管给我打电话。我很乐意帮忙。

ex.en: Would you oblige me with some information?
ex.cn: 拜托您给我透露些消息好吗？

ex.en: Oblige me by keeping your suspicions to yourself.
ex.cn: 拜托你不要把你的怀疑声张出去。

senses.def: used when you are expressing thanks or asking politely for sth, to show that you are grateful to sb

ex.en: I'm much obliged to you for helping us.
ex.cn: 承蒙相助，本人不胜感激。

ex.en: I'd be obliged if you would keep this to yourself.
ex.cn: 如蒙保守这个秘密，我将感激不尽。

senses.def: very willing to help

ex.en: They were very obliging and offered to wait for us.
ex.cn: 他们非常热情，主动提出等候我们。

senses.def: not expressed or done in a direct way
senses.chn: 间接的；不直截了当的；拐弯抹角的

ex.en: an oblique reference/approach/comment
ex.cn: 隐约提及；间接途径；婉转的评论

senses.def: sloping at an angle
an angle that is not an angle of 90°
to remove all signs of sth, either by destroying or covering it completely

ex.en: The building was completely obliterated by the bomb.
ex.cn: 炸弹把那座建筑物彻底摧毁了。

ex.en: The snow had obliterated their footprints.
ex.cn: 白雪覆盖了他们的足迹。

ex.en: Everything that happened that night was obliterated from his memory.
ex.cn: 那天夜里发生的一切都从他的记忆中消失了。

senses.def: a state in which you are not aware of what is happening around you, usually because you are unconscious or asleep

ex.en: He often drinks himself into oblivion.
ex.cn: 他常常喝酒喝得不省人事。

ex.en: Sam longed for the oblivion of sleep.
ex.cn: 萨姆恨不得一睡不醒，了无心事。

senses.def: the state in which sb/sth has been forgotten and is no longer famous or important

ex.en: An unexpected victory saved him from political oblivion.
ex.cn: 一次意外的胜利使得他在政治上不再默默无闻。

ex.en: Most of his inventions have been consigned to oblivion.
ex.cn: 他的大部分发明都湮没无闻了。

senses.def: a state in which sth has been completely destroyed

ex.en: Hundreds of homes were bombed into oblivion during the first weeks of the war.
ex.cn: 在战争的最初几周内，数以百计的房屋被炸毁。

senses.def: not aware of sth

ex.en: He drove off, oblivious of the damage he had caused.
ex.cn: 他驾车而去，没有注意到他所造成的损害。

ex.en: You eventually become oblivious to the noise.
ex.cn: 你终究会变得不在意吵闹声的。

senses.def: an oblong shape has four straight sides, two of which are longer than the other two, and four angles of 90°
used to describe any shape that is longer than it is wide
senses.chn: 椭圆形的；椭圆体的；长方形的

ex.en: an oblong melon
ex.cn: 椭圆形的瓜

senses.def: strong public criticism
senses.chn: 公开的抨击；公开的谴责；辱骂

senses.def: loss of respect and honour
extremely unpleasant, especially in a way that offends people
senses.chn: 极讨厌的；可憎的；令人作呕的

ex.en: obnoxious behaviour
ex.cn: 讨厌的行为

ex.en: a thoroughly obnoxious little man
ex.cn: 可恶至极的家伙

ex.en: obnoxious odours
ex.cn: 难闻的气味

senses.def: or best offer (used in small advertisements to show that sth may be sold at a lower price than the price that has been asked)

ex.en: $800 obo
ex.cn: 800 美元（可议价）

senses.def: a musical instrument of the woodwind group. It is shaped like a pipe and has a double reed at the top that you blow into.
a person who plays the oboe
connected with sex in a way that most people find offensive

ex.en: obscene gestures/language/books
ex.cn: 淫秽的姿势／语言／书籍

ex.en: an obscene phone call (= in which sb says obscene things)
ex.cn: 色情骚扰电话

senses.def: extremely large in size or amount in a way that most people find unacceptable and offensive
senses.chn: （数量等）大得惊人的，骇人听闻的

ex.en: He earns an obscene amount of money.
ex.cn: 他赚钱多得吓人。

ex.en: It's obscene to spend so much on food when millions are starving.
ex.cn: 当数以百万的人忍饥挨饿时，饮食上挥霍无度是天理难容的。

senses.def: obscene language or behaviour
senses.chn: 淫秽的语言；下流的行为

ex.en: The editors are being prosecuted for obscenity.
ex.cn: 几个编辑因刊载污秽文字而被起诉。

ex.en: the laws on obscenity
ex.cn: 禁止淫秽的言语及行为的法规

senses.def: an obscene word or act

ex.en: She screamed a string of obscenities at the judge.
ex.cn: 她冲着法官高声骂了一连串的脏话。

senses.def: the practice of deliberately preventing sb from understanding or discovering sth
senses.chn: 故弄玄虚；蒙蔽主义；蒙骗政策

senses.def: not well known

ex.en: an obscure German poet
ex.cn: 一个名不见经传的德国诗人

ex.en: He was born around 1650 but his origins remain obscure.
ex.cn: 他生于 1650 年前后，但身世不详。

senses.def: difficult to understand

ex.en: I found her lecture very obscure.
ex.cn: 我觉得她的讲座非常费解。

ex.en: For some obscure reason, he failed to turn up.
ex.cn: 他莫名其妙地没有如期露面。

senses.def: to make it difficult to see, hear or understand sth

ex.en: The view was obscured by fog.
ex.cn: 雾中景色朦胧。

ex.en: We mustn't let these minor details obscure the main issue.
ex.cn: 我们不能让枝节问题掩盖主要问题。

senses.def: the state in which sb/sth is not well known or has been forgotten

ex.en: The actress was only 17 when she was plucked from obscurity and made a star.
ex.cn: 这个演员受到提携从无名少女一跃成为明星时年仅 17 岁。

ex.en: He spent most of his life working in obscurity.
ex.cn: 他在默默无闻的工作中度过了大半生。

senses.def: the quality of being difficult to understand; something that is difficult to understand

ex.en: The course teaches students to avoid ambiguity and obscurity of expression.
ex.cn: 这门课程教学生避免表达上的模棱两可、含混不清。

ex.en: a speech full of obscurities
ex.cn: 一篇晦涩难懂的演说

senses.def: the state of being dark
funeral ceremonies

ex.en: state obsequies
ex.cn: 国葬

senses.def: trying too hard to please sb, especially sb who is important

ex.en: an obsequious manner
ex.cn: 谄媚的态度

senses.def: that can be seen or noticed
senses.chn: 能看得到的；能察觉到的

ex.en: observable differences
ex.cn: 可以察觉到的差异

ex.en: Similar trends are observable in mainland Europe.
ex.cn: 类似的趋势在欧洲大陆也能见到。

senses.def: the practice of obeying a law, celebrating a festival or behaving according to a particular custom
senses.chn: （对法律、习俗的）遵守，奉行；（节日的）庆祝

ex.en: observance of the law
ex.cn: 守法

ex.en: a strict observance of the Sabbath
ex.cn: 对安息日的严格遵守

senses.def: an act performed as part of a religious or traditional ceremony
senses.chn: 宗教（或传统节日）的仪式

ex.en: religious observances
ex.cn: 宗教仪式

senses.def: good at noticing things around you
senses.chn: 善于观察的；观察力敏锐的

ex.en: Observant walkers may see red deer along this stretch of the road.
ex.cn: 观察敏锐的步行者能在这一路段看到赤鹿。

ex.en: How very observant of you!
ex.cn: 你真有眼力！

senses.def: careful to obey religious laws and customs
senses.chn: 谨慎遵守教规和习俗的

senses.def: the act of watching sb/sth carefully for a period of time, especially to learn sth

ex.en: Most information was collected by direct observation of the animals' behaviour.
ex.cn: 大部分信息都是通过直接观察动物的行为收集到的。

ex.en: results based on scientific observations
ex.cn: 根据科学观测得来的结果

ex.en: We managed to escape observation (= we were not seen).
ex.cn: 我们设法避开了人们的注意。

ex.en: The suspect is being kept under observation (= watched closely by the police).
ex.cn: 嫌疑人正受到监视。

ex.en: She has outstanding powers of observation (= the ability to notice things around her).
ex.cn: 她有超人的观察力。

ex.en: an observation post/tower (= a place from where sb, especially an enemy, can be watched)
ex.cn: 瞭望哨；瞭望塔

senses.def: a comment, especially based on sth you have seen, heard or read
senses.chn: （尤指据所见、所闻、所读而作的）评论

ex.en: He began by making a few general observations about the report.
ex.cn: 开头他先对这个报告作了几点概括性的评论。

ex.en: She has some interesting observations on possible future developments.
ex.cn: 她对未来可能的发展有一些饶有兴味的论述。

ex.en: A government spokesperson made a statement to the press.
ex.cn: 政府发言人向新闻界发表了一份声明。

ex.en: She made helpful comments on my work.
ex.cn: 她对我的工作提出了有益的意见。

ex.en: the announcement of a peace agreement
ex.cn: 和平协议公告

ex.en: He made a number of rude remarks about the food.
ex.cn: 他对这食物作了许多无礼的评论。

senses.def: a coach/car on a train with large windows, designed to give passengers a good view of the passing landscape
senses.chn: 观光车厢，游览车厢（火车车厢，有大窗）

senses.def: a special building from which scientists watch the stars, the weather, etc.
to see or notice sb/sth

ex.en: Have you observed any changes lately?
ex.cn: 最近你注意到什么变化没有？

ex.en: All the characters in the novel are closely observed (= seem like people in real life).
ex.cn: 小说中的人物个个栩栩如生。

ex.en: The police observed a man enter the bank.
ex.cn: 警察注意到一个男人走进了银行。

ex.en: They observed him entering the bank.
ex.cn: 他们看见他走进银行。

ex.en: She observed that all the chairs were already occupied.
ex.cn: 她发现所有的椅子都有人坐了。

ex.en: He was observed to follow her closely.
ex.cn: 有人看到他紧跟着她。

senses.def: to watch sb/sth carefully, especially to learn more about them

ex.en: I felt he was observing everything I did.
ex.cn: 我觉得他正在注视着我做的每一件事。

ex.en: The patients were observed over a period of several months.
ex.cn: 这些病人被观察了数月之久。

ex.en: He observes keenly, but says little.
ex.cn: 他观察敏锐，但言语寥寥。

ex.en: They observed how the parts of the machine fitted together.
ex.cn: 他们观看了机器零件的组装过程。

ex.en: If you look carefully you can just see our house from here.
ex.cn: 你要是仔细看，从这里就可以看见我们的房子。

ex.en: She looked at me and smiled.
ex.cn: 她看了看我，笑了。

senses.def: to make a remark

ex.en: She observed that it was getting late.
ex.cn: 她说天色晚了。

senses.def: to obey rules, laws, etc.

ex.en: Will the rebels observe the ceasefire?
ex.cn: 叛乱者会遵守停火协议吗？

ex.en: The crowd observed a minute's silence (= were silent for one minute) in memory of those who had died.
ex.cn: 众人为死者默哀一分钟。

senses.def: to celebrate festivals, birthdays, etc.

ex.en: Do they observe Christmas?
ex.cn: 他们过不过圣诞节？

senses.def: a person who watches sb/sth

ex.en: According to observers, the plane exploded shortly after take-off.
ex.cn: 据目击者说，飞机起飞后不久就爆炸了。

ex.en: To the casual observer (= somebody who does not pay much attention), the system appears confusing.
ex.cn: 乍看起来，这个系统好像条理不清。

ex.en: Police have appealed for witnesses to the accident.
ex.cn: 警方呼吁这起事故的目击者出来作证。

ex.en: According to observers, the plane exploded shortly after take-off.
ex.cn: 据目击者说，飞机起飞后不久就爆炸了。

ex.en: A crowd of onlookers gathered at the scene of the crash.
ex.cn: 在撞车地点聚集了一大群围观者。

ex.en: Police asked passers-by if they had witnessed the accident.
ex.cn: 警察询问过路的人是否目击了这次事故。

senses.def: a person who attends a meeting, lesson, etc. to listen and watch but not to take part

ex.en: A team of British officials were sent as observers to the conference.
ex.cn: 一组英国官员被派去做大会观察员。

senses.def: a person who watches and studies particular events, situations, etc. and is therefore considered to be an expert on them

ex.en: a royal observer
ex.cn: 王室观察家

senses.def: to completely fill your mind so that you cannot think of anything else, in a way that is not normal

ex.en: He's obsessed by computers.
ex.cn: 他迷上了电脑。

ex.en: She's completely obsessed with him.
ex.cn: 他让她神魂颠倒。

ex.en: The need to produce the most exciting newspaper story obsesses most journalists.
ex.cn: 大多数记者梦寐以求的就是要写出最撼动人心的新闻报道来。

senses.def: to be always talking or worrying about a particular thing, especially when this annoys other people

ex.en: I think you should try to stop obsessing about food.
ex.cn: 我看你该歇歇了，别没完没了地唠叨吃的东西。

senses.def: the state in which a person's mind is completely filled with thoughts of one particular thing or person in a way that is not normal

ex.en: Her fear of flying is bordering on obsession.
ex.cn: 她怕乘飞机几乎到了不可救药的地步。

ex.en: The media's obsession with the young prince continues.
ex.cn: 新闻媒体继续对小王子进行连篇累牍的报道。

senses.def: a person or thing that sb thinks about too much

ex.en: Fitness has become an obsession with him.
ex.cn: 他迷上了健身。

senses.def: thinking too much about one particular person or thing, in a way that is not normal
senses.chn: 痴迷的；迷恋的；耿耿于怀的

ex.en: She is obsessional about cleanliness.
ex.cn: 她有洁癖。

ex.en: obsessional behaviour
ex.cn: 痴迷的行为

senses.def: thinking too much about one particular person or thing, in a way that is not normal
senses.chn: 着迷的；迷恋的；难以释怀的

ex.en: He's becoming more and more obsessive about punctuality.
ex.cn: 他对守时要求越来越过分了。

ex.en: an obsessive attention to detail
ex.cn: 过分注重细枝末节

senses.def: a person whose mind is filled with thoughts of one particular thing or person so that they cannot think of anything else
a type of dark rock that looks like glass and comes from volcanoes
the state of becoming old-fashioned and no longer useful

ex.en: products with built-in/planned obsolescence (= designed not to last long so that people will have to buy new ones)
ex.cn: 内在／计划陈旧产品（故意设计成不耐使用而迫使人购买新的产品）

senses.def: no longer used because sth new has been invented

ex.en: obsolete technology
ex.cn: 过时技术

ex.en: With technological changes many traditional skills have become obsolete.
ex.cn: 随着技术的革新，许多传统技艺已被淘汰。

senses.def: a situation, an event, etc. that makes it difficult for you to do or achieve sth

ex.en: A lack of qualifications can be a major obstacle to finding a job.
ex.cn: 学历不足可能成为谋职的主要障碍。

ex.en: So far, we have managed to overcome all the obstacles that have been placed in our path.
ex.cn: 到目前为止，我们已设法排除了前进道路上的一切人为障碍。

senses.def: an object that is in your way and that makes it difficult for you to move forward

ex.en: The area was full of streams and bogs and other natural obstacles.
ex.cn: 此地遍布小溪、泥潭和其他天然障碍。

senses.def: a fence, etc. for a horse to jump over
a series of objects that people taking part in a race have to climb over, under, through, etc.
a series of difficulties that people have to deal with in order to achieve a particular aim
an area of land with many objects that are difficult to climb, jump over or go through, which is used, especially by soldiers, for improving physical skills and strength
a race in which the people taking part have to climb over, under, through, etc. various objects
a doctor who is trained in obstetrics
the branch of medicine concerned with the birth of children
refusing to change your opinions, way of behaving, etc. when other people try to persuade you to; showing this

ex.en: He can be very obstinate when he wants to be!
ex.cn: 他的犟劲儿一上来，简直执拗得要命！

ex.en: her obstinate refusal to comply with their request
ex.cn: 她拒不服从他们的要求

senses.def: difficult to get rid of or deal with
senses.chn: 棘手的；难以去除的；难以对付的

ex.en: the obstinate problem of unemployment
ex.cn: 失业这个棘手的问题

ex.en: an obstinate stain
ex.cn: 顽固斑渍

senses.def: noisy and difficult to control
senses.chn: 喧闹的；桀骜不驯的；任性的

senses.def: to block a road, an entrance, a passage, etc. so that sb/sth cannot get through, see past, etc.

ex.en: You can't park here, you're obstructing my driveway.
ex.cn: 你不能在这里停车，你挡住了我家的车道。

ex.en: First check that the accident victim doesn't have an obstructed airway.
ex.cn: 首先要确保事故受伤者的气道通畅。

ex.en: The pillar obstructed our view of the stage.
ex.cn: 柱子挡着，我们看不见舞台。

senses.def: to prevent sb/sth from doing sth or making progress, especially when this is done deliberately

ex.en: They were charged with obstructing the police in the course of their duty.
ex.cn: 他们被指控妨碍警察执行公务。

ex.en: terrorists attempting to obstruct the peace process
ex.cn: 企图阻碍和平进程的恐怖分子

senses.def: to tell a lie or to do sth in order to prevent the police, etc. from finding out the truth about a crime
the fact of trying to prevent sth/sb from making progress

ex.en: the obstruction of justice
ex.cn: 妨碍司法公正

ex.en: He was arrested for obstruction of a police officer in the execution of his duty.
ex.cn: 他因妨碍警察执行公务而被逮捕。

senses.def: the fact of blocking a road, an entrance, a passage, etc.

ex.en: obstruction of the factory gates
ex.cn: 对工厂大门的堵塞

ex.en: The abandoned car was causing an obstruction.
ex.cn: 这辆被遗弃的汽车堵住了道路。

senses.def: something that blocks a road, an entrance, etc.

ex.en: It is my job to make sure that all pathways are clear of obstructions.
ex.cn: 保证所有的道路通畅是我的职责。

senses.def: something that blocks a passage or tube in your body; a medical condition resulting from this

ex.en: He had an operation to remove an obstruction in his throat.
ex.cn: 他做了手术，取出喉头的阻塞物。

ex.en: bowel/intestinal obstruction
ex.cn: 肠梗阻

senses.def: the offence of unfairly preventing a player of the other team from moving to get the ball
the practice of trying to prevent a parliament or committee from making progress, passing laws, etc.
senses.chn: （对议会或委员会工作的）阻挠行为，妨碍

senses.def: trying to prevent sb/sth from making progress

ex.en: Of course she can do it. She's just being deliberately obstructive.
ex.cn: 这事她当然能做。她只是在刻意阻挠罢了。

senses.def: connected with a passage, tube, etc. in your body that has become blocked

ex.en: obstructive lung disease
ex.cn: 肺阻塞疾病

senses.def: to tell a lie or to do sth in order to prevent the police, etc. from finding out the truth about a crime
to get sth, especially by making an effort

ex.en: to obtain advice/information/permission
ex.cn: 得到忠告／信息／许可

ex.en: I finally managed to obtain a copy of the report.
ex.cn: 我终于设法弄到了这份报告的一个副本。

ex.en: To obtain the overall score, add up the totals in each column.
ex.cn: 要得出总计得分，就把各栏的小计加起来。

senses.def: to exist

ex.en: These conditions no longer obtain.
ex.cn: 这些条件不再适用。

senses.def: that can be obtained

ex.en: Full details are obtainable from any post office.
ex.cn: 详情可至任何邮局索取。

senses.def: to become or make sth/yourself noticed, especially in a way that is not wanted

ex.en: Music from the next room obtruded upon his thoughts.
ex.cn: 隔壁的音乐声打扰了他的思绪。

senses.def: noticeable in an unpleasant way
senses.chn: 扎眼的；过分炫耀的；显眼的

ex.en: The sofa would be less obtrusive in a paler colour.
ex.cn: 沙发的颜色再浅一点就不那么扎眼了。

ex.en: They tried to ensure that their presence was not too obtrusive.
ex.cn: 他们尽量做到在场时不引人注目。

senses.def: slow or unwilling to understand sth
senses.chn: 迟钝的；愚蠢的；态度勉强的

ex.en: Are you being deliberately obtuse?
ex.cn: 你是不是故意装傻？

senses.def: an angle between 90° and 180°
the opposite of sth

ex.en: The obverse of love is hate.
ex.cn: 爱的反面是恨。

senses.def: the side of a coin or medal that has the head or main design on it
to remove a problem or the need for sth

ex.en: This new evidence obviates the need for any further enquiries.
ex.cn: 这项新证据排除了继续调查的必要。

senses.def: easy to see or understand
senses.chn: 明显的；显然的；易理解的

ex.en: It was obvious to everyone that the child had been badly treated.
ex.cn: 人人一看便知那个孩子受过虐待。

ex.en: It's obvious from what she said that something is wrong.
ex.cn: 根据她所说的，显然是出问题了。

ex.en: I know you don't like her but try not to make it so obvious.
ex.cn: 我知道你不喜欢她，但尽量别表现得那么明显。

ex.en: He agreed with obvious pleasure.
ex.cn: 他同意了，显然很高兴。

ex.en: For obvious reasons, I'd prefer not to give my name.
ex.cn: 因为显而易见的原因，我不愿披露自己的姓名。

ex.en: The reasons for this decision were not immediately obvious.
ex.cn: 作出这一决定的理由暂时还不清楚。

senses.def: that most people would think of or agree to

ex.en: She was the obvious choice for the job.
ex.cn: 她是这一工作的当然人选。

ex.en: There's no obvious solution to the problem.
ex.cn: 这个问题尚无公认的解决办法。

ex.en: This seemed the most obvious thing to do.
ex.cn: 这似乎是最顺理成章的做法。

senses.def: not interesting, new or showing imagination; unnecessary because it is clear to everyone
senses.chn: 平淡无奇的；无创意的；因显而易见而不必要的

ex.en: The ending was pretty obvious.
ex.cn: 结尾十分平淡。

ex.en: I may be stating the obvious but without more money the project cannot survive.
ex.cn: 我这话可能多余，但是不投入更多资金，项目就难以为继。

senses.def: used when giving information that you expect other people to know already or agree with
senses.chn: （用于陈述认为别人已知道或希望别人同意的事）显然，明显地

ex.en: Obviously, we don't want to spend too much money.
ex.cn: 很明显，我们不想花太多的钱。

ex.en: Diet and exercise are obviously important.
ex.cn: 显然，饮食和运动是重要的。

senses.def: used to say that a particular situation or fact is easy to see or understand
senses.chn: （用于说明某种情况或事实）显而易见，明显，不言而喻

ex.en: He was obviously drunk.
ex.cn: 他显然是喝醉了。

ex.en: They're obviously not coming.
ex.cn: 他们显然不会来了。

ex.en: 'I didn't realise it was a formal occasion.' 'Obviously!' (= I can see by the way you are dressed)
ex.cn: “我没想到这是个正式场合。” “看得出来！”（= 看你的衣着就知道）

senses.def: obviously
a small egg-shaped musical instrument that you blow into, with holes for the fingers
senses.chn: 奥卡里纳，小鹅笛，陶笛（管身椭圆形）

senses.def: a particular time when sth happens

ex.en: on this/that occasion
ex.cn: 这次；那次

ex.en: I've met him on several occasions.
ex.cn: 我曾见过他几次。

ex.en: I can remember very few occasions when he had to cancel because of ill health.
ex.cn: 我记得他因为健康不佳而被迫取消的情况绝无仅有。

ex.en: They have been seen together on two separate occasions.
ex.cn: 他们有两次被人看见在一起。

ex.en: On one occasion, she called me in the middle of the night.
ex.cn: 有一次她深更半夜打电话给我。

ex.en: He used the occasion to announce further tax cuts.
ex.cn: 他利用这个机会宣布再次减税。

senses.def: a special event, ceremony or celebration
senses.chn: 特别的事情（或仪式、庆典）

ex.en: a great/memorable/happy occasion
ex.cn: 伟大的／难忘的／欢乐的庆典

ex.en: Turn every meal into a special occasion.
ex.cn: 要把每一顿饭都弄得特别一些。

ex.en: They marked the occasion (= celebrated it) with an open-air concert.
ex.cn: 他们举办了露天音乐会来庆祝。

ex.en: Their wedding turned out to be quite an occasion.
ex.cn: 他们的婚礼办得相当隆重。

ex.en: He was presented with the watch on the occasion of his retirement.
ex.cn: 他在退休仪式上获赠这块手表。

senses.def: a suitable time for sth

ex.en: It should have been an occasion for rejoicing, but she could not feel any real joy.
ex.cn: 原本应该是高兴的时刻，她却丝毫未感到快乐。

ex.en: I'll speak to him about it if the occasion arises (= if I get a chance).
ex.cn: 有机会的话，我要跟他谈谈这件事。

senses.def: a reason or cause

ex.en: I've had no occasion to visit him recently.
ex.cn: 我最近无缘去拜访他。

ex.en: Her death was the occasion of mass riots.
ex.cn: 她的逝世引发了大规模的骚乱。

ex.en: I'm willing to go to court over this if the occasion arises (= if it becomes necessary).
ex.cn: 如果必要的话，我愿意就此出庭。

senses.def: sometimes but not often

ex.en: He has been known on occasion to lose his temper.
ex.cn: 大家都知道他有时会发脾气。

senses.def: a feeling or understanding that an event is important or special

ex.en: Candles on the table gave the evening a sense of occasion.
ex.cn: 桌上点了一些蜡烛，使得那个晚上有一种特别的气氛。

senses.def: to cause sth

ex.en: The flight delay was occasioned by the need for a further security check.
ex.cn: 这次航班的延误是由于必须做进一步的安全检查。

ex.en: The decision occasioned us much anxiety.
ex.cn: 这个决定让我们忧虑不堪。

senses.def: happening or done sometimes but not often

ex.en: He works for us on an occasional basis.
ex.cn: 他在我们这里做临时工。

ex.en: I enjoy the occasional glass of wine.
ex.cn: 我喜欢偶尔喝一杯葡萄酒。

ex.en: He spent five years in Paris, with occasional visits to Italy.
ex.cn: 他在巴黎待过五年，偶尔去一去意大利。

ex.en: an occasional smoker (= a person who smokes, but not often)
ex.cn: 偶尔吸烟的人

senses.def: sometimes but not often

ex.en: We occasionally meet for a drink after work.
ex.cn: 我们下班后偶尔相聚小酌。

ex.en: This type of allergy can very occasionally be fatal.
ex.cn: 这类过敏症在极个别情况下有可能是致命的。

senses.def: a small light table that is easy to move, used for different things at different times
to cover or block sth

ex.en: an occluded artery
ex.cn: 闭塞的动脉

senses.def: connected with magic powers and things that cannot be explained by reason or science
senses.chn: 神秘的；玄妙的；超自然的；不可思议的

ex.en: occult practices
ex.cn: 神秘的习俗

senses.def: everything connected with occult practices, etc.

ex.en: He's interested in witchcraft and the occult.
ex.cn: 他对巫术魔法情有独钟。

senses.def: a person who is involved in the occult
the act of living in or using a building, room, piece of land, etc.
senses.chn: （房屋、土地等的）占用，使用，居住

ex.en: Prices are based on full occupancy of an apartment.
ex.cn: 公寓租金按整套租用计算。

ex.en: to be in sole occupancy
ex.cn: 单独占用

senses.def: a person who lives or works in a particular house, room, building, etc.
senses.chn: （房屋、建筑等的）使用者，居住者

ex.en: All outstanding bills will be paid by the previous occupants.
ex.cn: 所有未支付的账单都将由前住户偿付。

senses.def: a person who is in a vehicle, seat, etc. at a particular time

ex.en: The car was badly damaged but the occupants were unhurt.
ex.cn: 汽车严重损坏，但车内人员安然无恙。

senses.def: a job or profession

ex.cn: 我那只狗的照片

ex.en: a map of India
ex.cn: 印度地图

senses.def: used to say what sb/sth is, consists of, or contains
senses.chn: （用于表示性质、组成或涵盖）即，由…组成

ex.en: the city of Dublin
ex.cn: 都柏林市

ex.en: the issue of housing
ex.cn: 住房问题

ex.en: a crowd of people
ex.cn: 一群人

ex.en: a glass of milk
ex.cn: 一杯牛奶

senses.def: used with measurements and expressions of time, age, etc.
senses.chn: （用于表示计量、时间或年龄等）

ex.en: 2 kilos of potatoes
ex.cn: 两公斤马铃薯

ex.en: an increase of 2%
ex.cn: 2% 的增长

ex.en: a girl of 12
ex.cn: 12 岁的女孩

ex.en: the fourth of July
ex.cn: 七月四日

ex.en: the year of his birth
ex.cn: 他出生的那一年

ex.en: We would often have a walk of an evening.
ex.cn: 我们过去常在晚上散步。

senses.def: used to show sb/sth belongs to a group, often after some, a few, etc.
senses.chn: （常用在 some、a few 等词语之后，表示人或物的所属）属于…的

ex.en: some of his friends
ex.cn: 他的几位朋友

ex.en: a few of the problems
ex.cn: 其中的几个问题

ex.en: the most famous of all the stars
ex.cn: 最知名的一位明星

senses.def: used to show the position of sth/sb in space or time
senses.chn: （表示人或事的时空位置）在，当

ex.en: just north of Detroit
ex.cn: 就在底特律以北

ex.en: at the time of the revolution
ex.cn: 在革命的年代

ex.en: at a quarter of eleven tonight (= 10.45 p.m.)
ex.cn: 在今晚十一点差一刻

senses.def: used after nouns formed from verbs. The noun after 'of' can be either the object or the subject of the action.
senses.chn: （用于由动词转化的名词之后，of 之后的名词可以是受动者，也可以是施动者）

ex.en: the arrival of the police (= they arrive)
ex.cn: 警察的到来

ex.en: criticism of the police (= they are criticized)
ex.cn: 对警察的批评

ex.en: fear of the dark
ex.cn: 对黑暗的惧怕

ex.en: the howling of the wind
ex.cn: 狂风的呼啸

senses.def: used after some verbs before mentioning sb/sth involved in the action
senses.chn: （用于某些动词后，后接动作所涉及的人或事）

ex.en: to deprive sb of sth
ex.cn: 剥夺某人的东西

ex.en: He was cleared of all blame.
ex.cn: 他所受的一切责难都澄清了。

ex.en: Think of a number, any number.
ex.cn: 想一个数字，随便一个。

senses.def: used after some adjectives before mentioning sb/sth that a feeling relates to
senses.chn: （用于某些形容词后，后接与感情相关的人或事）因为，由于

ex.en: to be proud of sth
ex.cn: 为某事自豪

senses.def: used to give your opinion of sb's behaviour
senses.chn: （用于对某人的行为发表看法）

ex.en: It was kind of you to offer.
ex.cn: 感谢你的好意。

senses.def: used when one noun describes a second one
senses.chn: （用于一个名词修饰另一个名词时）

ex.en: Where's that idiot of a boy (= the boy that you think is stupid)?
ex.cn: 那个傻小子在哪儿？

senses.def: used before a noun to say that sth is very surprising
senses.chn: （用于名词前，表示某事着实令人吃惊）竟然，偏偏

ex.en: I'm surprised that you of all people should say that.
ex.cn: 你竟然那么说，真让我吃惊！

senses.def: used to express anger

ex.en: Of all the nerve!
ex.cn: 竟然如此厚颜无耻！

senses.def: if you talk about a person being of a certain age, you mean that they are no longer young but not yet old
senses.chn: 不算年轻的；年纪不轻的；中年的

ex.en: The show appeals to an audience of a certain age.
ex.cn: 这个节目中年观众感兴趣。

senses.def: used in polite expressions to describe sb as 'very old'

ex.en: He was a man of advanced years.
ex.cn: 他年事已高。

ex.en: Even at my advanced age I still know how to enjoy myself!
ex.cn: 我虽说是黄昏暮年，也还懂得如何找乐儿！

senses.def: of a high quality or degree; of the highest quality or greatest degree
senses.chn: 高质量的；高品质的；一流的

ex.en: The job requires diplomatic skills of a high order.
ex.cn: 这项工作要求高超的外交技巧。

ex.en: She was a snob of the first order.
ex.cn: 她是天字第一号势利鬼。

senses.def: not as good as it could be
senses.chn: 不怎么样，徒有其名（指不如本应有的那么好）

ex.en: You're making progress of a kind.
ex.cn: 你也算是有点进步的。

senses.def: very similar

ex.en: They're two of a kind—both workaholics!
ex.cn: 他们俩一个样，都是工作狂！

senses.def: used before a noun to say that sth is very surprising
senses.chn: （用于名词前，表示某事着实令人吃惊）竟然，偏偏

ex.en: I'm surprised that you of all people should say that.
ex.cn: 你竟然那么说，真让我吃惊！

senses.def: when you say of all people, you are emphasizing that sb is the person you would most or least expect to do sth

ex.en: She of all people should know the answer to that.
ex.cn: 在所有的人中，她是最应知道那个问题的答案的。

senses.def: that has ever existed
senses.chn: 自古以来；有史以来；从未有过

ex.en: Many rated him the best singer of all time.
ex.cn: 许多人认为他是有史以来最优秀的歌手。

senses.def: used to emphasize that what you are saying is true or correct
senses.chn: （强调所说的话属实或正确）当然

ex.en: 'Don't you like my mother?' 'Of course I do!'
ex.cn: “难道你不喜欢我母亲？” “当然喜欢！”

ex.en: 'Will you be there?' 'Course I will.'
ex.cn: “你会去那里吗？” “当然会。”

senses.def: used as a polite way of giving sb permission to do sth
senses.chn: （允许某人做某事的客气说法）当然

ex.en: 'Can I come, too?' 'Course you can.'
ex.cn: “我也可以来吗？” “当然可以。”

ex.en: 'Can I have one of those pens?' 'Of course—help yourself.'
ex.cn: “我能在那些笔中拿一支吗？” “当然，自己拿吧。”

senses.def: used as a polite way of agreeing with what sb has just said
senses.chn: （礼貌地同意某人刚说的话）当然

ex.en: 'I did all I could to help.' 'Of course,' he murmured gently.
ex.cn: “我尽全力帮忙了。” “当然。” 他轻声低语道。

senses.def: used to show that what you are saying is not surprising or is generally known or accepted
senses.chn: （表示所说的事不令人惊讶或具有普遍性）当然，自然

ex.en: Ben, of course, was the last to arrive.
ex.cn: 本当然是最后一个到的。

ex.en: Of course, there are other ways of doing this.
ex.cn: 当然还有别的方法做这件事。

ex.en: 'Is this the right room for the English class?' 'Yes, it is.'
ex.cn: “这是上英语课的教室吗？” “是的。”

ex.en: 'Can I borrow your dictionary?' 'Certainly.'(formal)
ex.cn: “我可以借用一下你的词典吗？” “当然可以。”（正式）

ex.en: 'Sure.'(informal)
ex.cn: “当然可以。”（非正式）

ex.en: 'Do you mind if I borrow your dictionary?' 'Not at all.'
ex.cn: “我借用一下你的词典行吗？” “没问题。”

senses.def: used to emphasize the fact that you are saying 'no'

ex.en: 'Are you going?' 'Of course not.'
ex.cn: “你要去吗？” “当然不去。”

ex.en: 'Do you mind?' 'No, of course not.'
ex.cn: “你介意吗？” “不，当然不介意。”

senses.def: willing to have sex with anyone
away from a place; at a distance in space or time
senses.chn: 离开（某处）；（在时间或空间上）距，离

ex.en: I called him but he ran off.
ex.cn: 我喊他，可他跑开了。

ex.en: Sarah's off in India somewhere.
ex.cn: 萨拉远在印度某地。

ex.en: I must be off soon (= leave).
ex.cn: 我得赶紧走了。

ex.en: Off you go!
ex.cn: 你走吧！

ex.en: Summer's not far off now.
ex.cn: 夏天已近在眼前了。

ex.en: A solution is still some way off.
ex.cn: 解决办法尚需时日。

senses.def: used to say that sth has been removed

ex.en: He's had his beard shaved off.
ex.cn: 他把胡子刮掉了。

ex.en: Take your coat off.
ex.cn: 脱了外衣吧。

ex.en: Don't leave the toothpaste with the top off.
ex.cn: 用完了牙膏别不盖盖。

senses.def: starting a race

ex.en: They're off (= the race has begun).
ex.cn: 他们起跑了。

senses.def: no longer going to happen; cancelled

ex.en: The wedding is off.
ex.cn: 婚礼被取消了。

senses.def: not connected or functioning

ex.en: The water is off.
ex.cn: 停水了。

ex.en: Make sure the TV is off.
ex.cn: 请注意关掉电视机。

senses.def: no longer available or being served

ex.en: Sorry, the duck is off.
ex.cn: 对不起，鸭子卖光了。

senses.def: away from work or duty

ex.en: She's off today.
ex.cn: 她今天休假。

ex.en: I've got three days off next week.
ex.cn: 我下周有三天休假。

ex.en: How many days did you take off?
ex.cn: 你休了几天假？

ex.en: I need some time off.
ex.cn: 我需要休息一段时间。

senses.def: taken from the price

ex.en: shoes with $20 off
ex.cn: 减价 20 美元的鞋

ex.en: All shirts have/are 10% off.
ex.cn: 衬衣全部减价 10%。

senses.def: behind or at the sides of the stage in a theatre
senses.chn: 在剧院舞台的后面（或旁边）

senses.def: used to say how much money sb has

ex.en: Families will be better off under the new law (= will have more money).
ex.cn: 这项新法律将使每个家庭的经济较前宽裕。

ex.en: They are both comfortably off (= have enough money to be able to buy what they want without worrying too much about the cost).
ex.cn: 他们俩的生活都很宽裕。

senses.def: to be in a better or worse situation

ex.en: She's better off without him.
ex.cn: 他不在身边她反倒更快乐。

ex.en: The weather was so bad we'd have been better off staying at home.
ex.cn: 天气太糟了，我们要是待在家里就好了。

ex.en: We can't be any worse off than we are already.
ex.cn: 我们的状况已经糟得不能再糟了。

senses.def: to have a particular amount of sth

ex.en: How are we off for coffee (= how much do we have)?
ex.cn: 我们还有多少咖啡？

senses.def: from time to time; now and again
senses.chn: 不时地；有时；断断续续地

ex.en: It rained on and off all day.
ex.cn: 雨断断续续地下了一整天。

senses.def: down or away from a place or at a distance in space or time
senses.chn: 从（某处）落下；离开；（时空上）离，距

ex.en: I fell off the ladder.
ex.cn: 我从梯子上跌了下来。

ex.en: Keep off the grass!
ex.cn: 勿践踏草坪！

ex.en: an island off the coast of Spain
ex.cn: 西班牙海岸附近的岛

ex.en: They were still 100 metres off the summit.
ex.cn: 他们距山顶还有 100 米远。

ex.en: Scientists are still a long way off finding a cure.
ex.cn: 科学家要找到一个治疗方法，还早着呢。

ex.en: We're getting right off the subject.
ex.cn: 我们完全离题了。

senses.def: leading away from sth, for example a road or room

ex.en: We live off Main Street.
ex.cn: 我们住在大街附近。

ex.en: There's a bathroom off the main bedroom.
ex.cn: 主卧室旁边有一个卫生间。

senses.def: used to say that sth has been removed

ex.en: You need to take the top off the bottle first!
ex.cn: 你得先把瓶盖子打开！

ex.en: I want about an inch off the back of my hair.
ex.cn: 我想把脑后的头发剪短约一英寸。

senses.def: away from work or duty

ex.en: He's had ten days off school.
ex.cn: 他有十天没上学了。

senses.def: away from a price

ex.en: They knocked £500 off the car.
ex.cn: 他们对这辆汽车杀价 500 英镑。

senses.def: off; from

ex.en: I got it off of my brother.
ex.cn: 这是我从我弟弟那里弄到的。

senses.def: not wanting or liking sth that you usually eat or use

ex.en: I'm off (= not drinking) alcohol for a week.
ex.cn: 我有一星期没喝酒了。

ex.en: He's finally off drugs (= he no longer takes them).
ex.cn: 他终于把毒戒了。

senses.def: no longer fresh enough to eat or drink

ex.en: This fish has gone off.
ex.cn: 这条鱼已变质了。

ex.en: The milk smells off.
ex.cn: 这奶的味道不对劲。

ex.en: It's off.
ex.cn: 那东西坏了。

senses.def: not polite or friendly

ex.en: He was a bit off with me this morning.
ex.cn: 他今天早晨对我有点冷淡。

senses.def: not acceptable
senses.chn: 不能接受；难以容忍；不行

ex.en: It's a bit off expecting us to work on Sunday.
ex.cn: 让我们星期天上班工作，那可不太行吧。

senses.def: the start of a race

ex.en: They're ready for the off.
ex.cn: 他们准备起跑了。

senses.def: to kill sb
not on; away from

ex.en: offstage
ex.cn: 幕后

ex.en: offload
ex.cn: 卸掉

senses.def: not being broadcast

ex.en: off-air recording
ex.cn: 非广播实况录制

senses.def: the inside parts of an animal, such as the heart and liver, cooked and eaten as food
completely wrong about sth

ex.en: If that's what you think, you're way off base.
ex.cn: 你如果那么想就全错了。

senses.def: not correct; wrong

ex.en: Your calculation is way off beam.
ex.cn: 你的计算完全错误。

senses.def: different from what most people expect
senses.chn: 不寻常的；不落俗套的；标新立异的

ex.en: offbeat humour
ex.cn: 另类的幽默

ex.en: an offbeat approach to interviewing
ex.cn: 别开生面的采访

senses.def: not on Broadway, New York's main theatre district
senses.chn: 不在百老汇的；外百老汇的

senses.def: unusual in some way and often by a new writer
senses.chn: 不落俗的；有新意的；出自新人之手的

senses.def: not exactly in the centre of sth
not in good health; looking or feeling ill/sick
senses.chn: 身体不舒服；气色不佳；不适

senses.def: an off-colour joke is one that people think is rude, usually because it is about sex
a piece of wood, paper, etc. that remains after the main piece has been cut
a day when you do not do things as well as usual
senses.chn: 不顺利的日子；倒霉的一天

senses.def: not at work

ex.en: an off-duty policeman
ex.cn: 休班警察

senses.def: an illegal act

ex.en: a criminal/serious/minor/sexual, etc. offence
ex.cn: 刑事罪、重罪、轻罪、性犯罪等

ex.en: a first offence (= the first time that sb has been found guilty of a crime)
ex.cn: 初犯

ex.en: a capital offence (= one for which sb may be punished by death)
ex.cn: 死罪

ex.en: He was not aware that he had committed an offence.
ex.cn: 他没有意识到自己犯罪了。

ex.en: an offence against society/humanity/the state
ex.cn: 妨害社会／人类／国家的罪行

ex.en: New legislation makes it an offence to carry guns.
ex.cn: 新法律规定持枪为犯罪行为。

senses.def: the act of upsetting or insulting sb

ex.en: I'm sure he meant no offence when he said that.
ex.cn: 我相信他那么说并无冒犯的意思。

ex.en: The photo may cause offence to some people.
ex.cn: 这张照片可能会引起一些人的反感。

ex.en: No one will take offence (= feel upset or insulted) if you leave early.
ex.cn: 你若早退谁也不会介意的。

ex.en: Don't be so quick to take offence.
ex.cn: 别动不动就生气。

senses.def: used to say that you do not mean to upset or insult sb by sth you say or do

ex.en: No offence, but I'd really like to be on my own.
ex.cn: 我无意冒犯，但我确实想自己一个人待着。

senses.def: to make sb feel upset because of sth you say or do that is rude or embarrassing

ex.en: They'll be offended if you don't go to their wedding.
ex.cn: 你若不参加他们的婚礼，他们会生气的。

ex.en: Neil did not mean to offend anybody with his joke.
ex.cn: 尼尔开那个玩笑并非想冒犯谁。

ex.en: A TV interviewer must be careful not to offend.
ex.cn: 电视采访者必须小心别得罪人。

senses.def: to seem unpleasant to sb

ex.en: The smell from the farm offended some people.
ex.cn: 农场散发的气味让一些人闻了不舒服。

ex.en: an ugly building that offends the eye
ex.cn: 一座丑陋碍眼的建筑物

senses.def: to commit a crime or crimes

ex.en: He started offending at the age of 16.
ex.cn: 他 16 岁就开始犯法。

senses.def: to be against what people believe is morally right
senses.chn: 违背（人情）；违反（常理）；有悖于

ex.en: comments that offend against people's religious beliefs
ex.cn: 有悖人民宗教信仰的评论

senses.def: a person who commits a crime

ex.en: a persistent/serious/violent, etc. offender
ex.cn: 惯犯、重犯、暴力犯等

ex.en: a young offender institution
ex.cn: 青少年罪犯管教所

senses.def: a person or thing that does sth wrong

ex.en: When it comes to pollution, the chemical industry is a major offender.
ex.cn: 谈到环境污染问题，化工产业是一大祸害。

senses.def: causing you to feel annoyed or upset; causing problems
senses.chn: 烦人的；令人不安的；惹麻烦的

ex.en: The offending paragraph was deleted.
ex.cn: 令某些人不悦的那段话已经删除。

ex.en: The traffic jam soon cleared once the offending vehicle had been removed.
ex.cn: 肇事车辆一经移走，交通拥堵很快就消除了。

senses.def: guilty of a crime

ex.en: The offending driver received a large fine.
ex.cn: 肇事司机被判以大额罚款。

senses.def: the members of a team whose main aim is to score points against the other team; a method of attack
senses.chn: （球队的）前锋，锋线队员；进攻方法；攻势

ex.en: The Redskins' offense is stronger than their defense.
ex.cn: 红皮队的进攻强于防守。

ex.en: He played offense for the Chicago Bulls.
ex.cn: 他在芝加哥公牛队打前锋。

senses.def: rude in a way that causes you to feel upset, insulted or annoyed
senses.chn: 冒犯的；得罪人的；无礼的

ex.en: offensive remarks
ex.cn: 冒犯的言论

ex.en: The programme contains language which some viewers may find offensive.
ex.cn: 节目里使用了某些观众可能认为是犯忌的语言。

ex.en: His comments were deeply offensive to a large number of single mothers.
ex.cn: 他的评论严重触怒了众多的单身母亲。

senses.def: extremely unpleasant
senses.chn: 极其讨厌的；令人不适的

ex.en: an offensive smell
ex.cn: 刺鼻的气味

ex.en: What a disgusting smell!
ex.cn: 这气味真难闻！

ex.en: She could smell his foul breath.
ex.cn: 她闻得到他的口臭。

ex.en: The stew looked revolting.
ex.cn: 这煨菜看上去令人作呕。

senses.def: connected with the act of attacking sb/sth

ex.en: an offensive war
ex.cn: 侵略战争

ex.en: offensive action
ex.cn: 进攻行动

ex.en: He was charged with carrying an offensive weapon.
ex.cn: 他被指控携带攻击性武器。

senses.def: connected with the team that has control of the ball; connected with the act of scoring points
senses.chn: 攻方的；进攻型的；攻击型的

ex.en: offensive play
ex.cn: 进攻打法

senses.def: a military operation in which large numbers of soldiers, etc. attack another country

ex.en: an air offensive
ex.cn: 空中攻击

ex.en: They launched the offensive on January 10.
ex.cn: 他们于 1 月 10 日发动了进攻。

senses.def: a series of actions aimed at achieving sth in a way that attracts a lot of attention
senses.chn: （引人注意的）系列行动；运动；攻势

ex.en: The government has launched a new offensive against crime.
ex.cn: 政府发动了新的打击犯罪攻势。

ex.en: a sales offensive
ex.cn: 销售攻势

ex.en: The public seems unconvinced by their latest charm offensive (= their attempt to make people like them).
ex.cn: 公众看起来并没被他们最近的魅力攻势所打动。

senses.def: to be attacking sb/sth rather than waiting for them to attack you
to start attacking sb/sth before they start attacking you
to say that you are willing to do sth for sb or give sth to sb

ex.en: Josie had offered her services as a guide.
ex.cn: 乔西曾表示愿意当向导。

ex.en: He offered some useful advice.
ex.cn: 他提出了一些有益的建议。

ex.en: I don't think they need help, but I think I should offer anyway.
ex.cn: 我想他们不需要帮助，但我认为我还是应该主动提出来。

ex.en: He offered $4 000 for the car.
ex.cn: 他出价 4 000 美元买这辆汽车。

ex.en: They decided to offer the job to Jo.
ex.cn: 他们决定把这份工作给乔。

ex.en: They decided to offer Jo the job.
